derivations.claim: Write $\mathscr S_\Phi$ for the finite anchored-shape list and $J_\Phi=\sum_{S\in\mathscr S_\Phi}\|\Phi(S)\|$. For each shape there are at most $|\Lambda|$ translates contained in $\Lambda$, so $\|H_\Lambda\|\le J_\Phi|\Lambda|$. By [F3], $H_\Lambda$ has real eigenvalues in $[-J_\Phi|\Lambda|,J_\Phi|\Lambda|]$. Therefore $q^{|\Lambda|}e^{-\beta J_\Phi|\Lambda|}\le Z_\Lambda(\beta)\le q^{|\Lambda|}e^{\beta J_\Phi|\Lambda|}$, and $p_\Lambda(\beta)$ is real and uniformly bounded.

For self-adjoint matrices $K,L$ on the same finite spin space, put $M_s=L+s(K-L)$. Apply [F2] to obtain $\frac{d}{ds}\log\operatorname{Tr}(e^{M_s})=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_s(K-L))$. The matrix $\rho_s$ is positive with trace one by [F3]; diagonalizing $\rho_s$ gives $|\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_s(K-L))|\le\|K-L\|$, since each unit eigenvector $v$ obeys $|\langle(K-L)v,v\rangle|\le\|K-L\|$. Integrating over $0\le s\le1$ proves $|\log\operatorname{Tr}(e^K)-\log\operatorname{Tr}(e^L)|\le\|K-L\|$. In particular, for self-adjoint Hamiltonians $H,H'$ on that same space, $|\log\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H})-\log\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H'})|\le\beta\|H-H'\|$.

Fix an integer block side $\ell\ge1$ and tile $Q_L$ by $N=\lfloor L/\ell\rfloor^d$ disjoint full $\ell$-cubes, leaving $E_L$ as the residual sites. The strips in the $d$ coordinate directions give $|E_L|\le d\ell L^{d-1}$ when $L\ge\ell$. Let $H_L^{\rm cut}$ be the sum of the free-boundary Hamiltonians of the full blocks, embedded into $\mathcal A_{Q_L}$, and zero on residual sites. An interaction term omitted from this cut either meets $E_L$ or crosses an internal grid plane. For each anchored shape, at most $M|E_L|$ translates meet $E_L$, because choosing a site of the shape and a residual site determines its anchor. For a fixed coordinate grid plane, at most $(r+1)L^{d-1}$ anchors can have a support crossing it, where $r=\lceil R\rceil$: the support's coordinate span is at most $r$, the anchor must lie in an interval of at most $r+1$ lattice sites, and each of the other $d-1$ anchor coordinates has at most $L$ choices. There are at most $dL/\ell$ internal planes. Thus $\|H_{Q_L}-H_L^{\rm cut}\|\le J_\Phi\bigl(M|E_L|+d(r+1)L^d/\ell\bigr)$.

The block Hamiltonians act on separate tensor factors. Diagonalize each block Hamiltonian using [F3]; tensor products of their eigenvectors and residual-site basis vectors form an orthonormal eigenbasis of $H_L^{\rm cut}$. Hence $\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H_L^{\rm cut}})=Z_{Q_\ell}(\beta)^Nq^{|E_L|}$. Step 1.2 and the residual-volume bound imply $\limsup_{L\to\infty}|p_{Q_L}(\beta)-p_{Q_\ell}(\beta)|\le\beta J_\Phi d(r+1)/\ell$.

For any $\epsilon>0$, choose $\ell$ so large that $2\beta J_\Phi d(r+1)/\ell<\epsilon/2$. The estimate in step 3.1 then makes $|p_{Q_L}(\beta)-p_{Q_{L'}}(\beta)|<\epsilon$ for all sufficiently large $L,L'$. The sequence is Cauchy in $\mathbb R$ and converges to a finite $p_\Phi(\beta)$ by step 1.1. The estimate also gives $|p_\Phi(\beta)-p_{Q_\ell}(\beta)|\le\beta J_\Phi d(r+1)/\ell$.

Let $(\Lambda_n)$ be van Hove and fix $\ell\ge1$. Use any fixed offset to tile $\mathbb Z^d$ by $\ell$-cubes, retain only cubes fully contained in $\Lambda_n$, and let $N_n$ be their number. Every residual site $x\in E_n:=\Lambda_n\setminus\bigcup B$ lies in a grid cube that also contains some $y\notin\Lambda_n$, so $\operatorname{dist}_\infty(x,\mathbb Z^d\setminus\Lambda_n)\le\ell-1$ and $E_n\subseteq\partial_\ell\Lambda_n$. Thus $|E_n|/|\Lambda_n|\to0$ and $N_n\ell^d=|\Lambda_n|-|E_n|$. Define $H_n^{\rm cut}$ to be the sum of the free-boundary Hamiltonians on the retained full cubes, embedded in $\mathcal A_{\Lambda_n}$, and zero on the residual sites. Any omitted interaction term either meets $E_n$, in which case its anchor lies in $\partial_{\ell+r}\Lambda_n$, or crosses a face between two retained cubes. For each retained cube, at most $2d(r+1)\ell^{d-1}$ anchor sites lie in its face layers wide enough for a support of range $r=\lceil R\rceil$ to cross a face; hence all internal-cut anchors number at most $2d(r+1)\ell^{d-1}N_n\le2d(r+1)|\Lambda_n|/\ell$. Since the norm sum over shapes at one anchor is $J_\Phi$, $\|H_{\Lambda_n}-H_n^{\rm cut}\|\le J_\Phi\bigl(|\partial_{\ell+r}\Lambda_n|+2d(r+1)|\Lambda_n|/\ell\bigr)$. Translation invariance makes every full-block partition function equal to $Z_{Q_\ell}$, and the zero residual Hamiltonian contributes $q^{|E_n|}$, so $\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda_n}(e^{-\beta H_n^{\rm cut}})=Z_{Q_\ell}^{N_n}q^{|E_n|}$. Divide the comparison from step 1.2 by $|\Lambda_n|$; the van Hove condition sends the fixed-width boundary term and $|E_n|/|\Lambda_n|$ to zero, while $N_n/|\Lambda_n|\to\ell^{-d}$. Therefore $\limsup_n|p_{\Lambda_n}(\beta)-p_{Q_\ell}(\beta)|\le2\beta J_\Phi d(r+1)/\ell$. Letting $\ell\to\infty$ and using step 4.1 proves $p_{\Lambda_n}(\beta)\to p_\Phi(\beta)$.

Put $\widetilde p_n:=|\Lambda_n|^{-1}\log\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda_n}(e^{-\beta(H_{\Lambda_n}+B_n)})$. Applying step 1.2 to the self-adjoint matrices $-\beta(H_{\Lambda_n}+B_n)$ and $-\beta H_{\Lambda_n}$ shows that $|\widetilde p_n-p_{\Lambda_n}(\beta)|\le\beta\|B_n\|/|\Lambda_n|$. This tends to zero by hypothesis, so step 5.1 gives $\widetilde p_n\to p_\Phi(\beta)$.

derivations.claim: For nonempty finite $\Lambda$, diagonalize $H_\Lambda$ using [F3], with eigenvalues $E_j$ and Gibbs weights $w_j=e^{-\beta E_j}/Z_\Lambda(\beta)$. Then $p_\Lambda(\beta)=|\Lambda|^{-1}\log\sum_j e^{-\beta E_j}$ is convex because $p_\Lambda''(\beta)=|\Lambda|^{-1}\bigl(\sum_jw_jE_j^2-(\sum_jw_jE_j)^2\bigr)=|\Lambda|^{-1}\sum_jw_j(E_j-\sum_kw_kE_k)^2\ge0$. Applying [F2] to $M(\beta)=-\beta H_\Lambda$ also gives $p_\Lambda'(\beta)=-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_{\Lambda,\beta}H_\Lambda)/|\Lambda|$.

For nonempty finite $\Lambda$, the measure $\mu_{\Lambda,\beta}$ assigns weight $w_j$ to each eigenvalue, combining weights when eigenvalues coincide, and is a probability measure because $\sum_jw_j=1$. For $t\in(0,\beta)$ and $e=e_\Phi(\beta)$, each eigenvalue $E\ge|\Lambda|(e+\epsilon)$ satisfies $e^{tE}\ge e^{t|\Lambda|(e+\epsilon)}$. Summing the corresponding weights gives $$ \mu_{\Lambda,\beta}\{E/|\Lambda|\ge e+\epsilon\}\le\exp\!\left(|\Lambda|\,[p_\Lambda(\beta-t)-p_\Lambda(\beta)-t(e+\epsilon)]\right). $$ The identity $\sum_jw_je^{tE_j}=Z_\Lambda(\beta-t)/Z_\Lambda(\beta)$ gives the displayed exponent.

Fix $h\in(0,\beta)$. Convexity in step 1.1 gives $(p_\Lambda(\beta)-p_\Lambda(\beta-h))/h\le p_\Lambda'(\beta)\le(p_\Lambda(\beta+h)-p_\Lambda(\beta))/h$. Along $\Lambda_n$, [F1] makes the two secants converge for fixed $h$ to the corresponding secants of $p_\Phi$. Letting $h\downarrow0$ and using differentiability at $\beta$ squeezes $p_{\Lambda_n}'(\beta)\to p_\Phi'(\beta)$; step 1.1 therefore proves $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_{\Lambda_n,\beta}H_{\Lambda_n})/|\Lambda_n|\to e_\Phi(\beta)$.

Differentiability and $e=-p_\Phi'(\beta)$ give $p_\Phi(\beta-t)-p_\Phi(\beta)=te+o(t)$ as $t\downarrow0$. Choose $t\in(0,\beta)$ so the remainder has magnitude at most $t\epsilon/2$. For all sufficiently large $n$, convergence in [F1] at $\beta-t$ and $\beta$ makes the exponent bracket in step 1.2 at most $-t\epsilon/4$. Thus the upper-tail probability is at most $e^{-t\epsilon|\Lambda_n|/4}$.

For the lower tail, if $E\le|\Lambda|(e-\epsilon)$ then $e^{-tE}\ge e^{-t|\Lambda|(e-\epsilon)}$. The same finite spectral sum gives $$ \mu_{\Lambda,\beta}\{E/|\Lambda|\le e-\epsilon\}\le\exp\!\left(|\Lambda|\,[p_\Lambda(\beta+t)-p_\Lambda(\beta)+t(e-\epsilon)]\right). $$ Since $p_\Phi(\beta+t)-p_\Phi(\beta)=-te+o(t)$, choose a possibly smaller fixed $t>0$ so the limiting bracket is at most $-t\epsilon/2$; for large $n$ the bracket is at most $-t\epsilon/4$. Let $t_+$ be the choice in step 2.2, let $t_-$ be this lower-tail choice, and set $c_0=\min(t_+,t_-)\epsilon/4>0$. Once $|\Lambda_n|\ge4\log2/c_0$, the sum of the two tail bounds $2e^{-c_0|\Lambda_n|}$ is at most $e^{-c_0|\Lambda_n|/2}$; hence $c_\epsilon=c_0/2$ works after increasing $n_0$.

derivations.claim: Diagonalize a local density matrix $\rho$ on a region of $m$ sites using [F3], with eigenvalues $\lambda_j\ge0$ summing to one and matrix dimension $D=q^m$, as supplied by [F4]. Then $S(\rho)=-\sum_{\lambda_j>0}\lambda_j\log\lambda_j\ge0$. For each positive $\lambda_j$, the scalar inequality $-\log x\ge1-x$ at $x=(D\lambda_j)^{-1}$ gives $\lambda_j\log(D\lambda_j)\ge\lambda_j-D^{-1}$. Summing over the positive eigenvalues yields $\log D-S(\rho)\ge1-r/D\ge0$, where $r$ is the rank. Thus $0\le S(\rho)\le m\log q$.

For each $S\in\mathscr S_\Phi$, let $N_S(L)$ count translations $x$ with $S+x\subseteq Q_L$. With $r=\lceil R\rceil$, $(L-2r)^d\le N_S(L)\le L^d$ for $L>2r$: every anchor at least $r$ sites from each face contains the whole support, and the anchor of every included term lies in $Q_L$. Translation invariance gives $\omega(\Phi(S+x))=\omega(\Phi(S))$. Therefore $\omega(H_{Q_L})/L^d=\sum_{S\in\mathscr S_\Phi}(N_S(L)/L^d)\omega(\Phi(S))\to\sum_{S\in\mathscr S_\Phi}\omega(\Phi(S))=u_\Phi(\omega)$.

Fix $\ell\ge1$ and tile $Q_L$ by $N=\lfloor L/\ell\rfloor^d$ disjoint $\ell$-cubes and residual sites $E_L$, where $|E_L|\le d\ell L^{d-1}$. Repeated use of [L1] subadditivity gives $S_{Q_L}(\omega)\le N S_{Q_\ell}(\omega)+S_{E_L}(\omega)$. By step 1.1 the last term is at most $|E_L|\log q$; if $E_L=\varnothing$, its scalar local density has entropy zero. Dividing by $L^d$ and taking the upper limit gives $\limsup_L S_{Q_L}(\omega)/L^d\le S_{Q_\ell}(\omega)/\ell^d$. Every ratio is at least their infimum over $\ell$, so the limit exists and equals that infimum.

On a fixed finite region, pointwise convergence of algebraic states gives convergence of all matrix coefficients of their density matrices by [F2] and [F4], hence convergence in operator norm. Ordered eigenvalues are continuous in that norm: the finite-dimensional min-max formula follows from an ordered orthonormal eigenbasis, since any $k$-dimensional subspace meets the span of the last $D-k+1$ eigenvectors, while the span of the first $k$ realizes the reverse bound; each Rayleigh quotient changes by at most the operator norm of the matrix difference. The function $-x\log x$, extended by $0$ at $x=0$, is continuous on $[0,1]$, so each $S_{Q_\ell}(\omega)$ is continuous under pointwise convergence. By step 2.1, $s(\omega)$ is the infimum of these continuous normalized local entropies and is upper semicontinuous. The energy density is a finite sum of local state evaluations by [F1], so it is continuous.

If a sequence of translation-invariant algebraic states converges pointwise to $\omega$, then for each fixed $x,A$ the equalities $\omega_n(\tau_x(A))=\omega_n(A)$ pass to the limit, so the invariant state set is closed. By [L2] every sequence in the full state space has a pointwise-convergent subsequence; the closed invariant subset is therefore sequentially compact.

derivations.claim: For any $\omega\in\mathcal S_{\mathrm{inv}}$, [F5] represents its restriction to $Q_L$ by a trace-one density matrix, and [L1] applies to that density. Writing $S_{Q_L}=-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_{Q_L}\log\rho_{Q_L})$ (dimensionless), the supplier's physical entropy is $k_{\mathrm B}S_{Q_L}$ and $T=(k_{\mathrm B}\beta)^{-1}$, so its inequality rearranges to $S_{Q_L}-\beta\omega(H_{Q_L})\le\log Z_{Q_L}(\beta)$. Divide by $L^d$ and use [F1]–[F2] to obtain $s(\omega)-\beta u_\Phi(\omega)\le p_\Phi(\beta)$. This is conditional on the stated finite-dimensional inequality [L1].

For each positive integer $\ell$, let $Q_\ell$ be one block, $H_\ell=H_{Q_\ell}$, and $\rho_\ell=e^{-\beta H_\ell}/Z_{Q_\ell}(\beta)$. Tile $\mathbb Z^d$ by blocks $B_k=\ell k+\{0,\ldots,\ell-1\}^d$, $k\in\mathbb Z^d$. For a finite region $\Lambda$, set $\rho_\Lambda=\bigotimes_{k:B_k\cap\Lambda\ne\varnothing}\operatorname{Tr}_{B_k\setminus\Lambda}(\rho_\ell^{(k)})$, where $\rho_\ell^{(k)}$ is the translated copy on $B_k$. This is a finite product; for $\Lambda=\varnothing$ the empty tensor product is the scalar unit density. Each nonempty block marginal is positive trace-one by [F3]–[F5].

If $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'$, then within each block the partial trace of $\operatorname{Tr}_{B_k\setminus\Lambda'}\rho_\ell^{(k)}$ over $(B_k\cap\Lambda')\setminus\Lambda$ equals $\operatorname{Tr}_{B_k\setminus\Lambda}\rho_\ell^{(k)}$: the coordinate formula in [F3] sums the same finite indices in either order. A block meeting $\Lambda'$ but not $\Lambda$ is traced over completely and contributes $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_\ell^{(k)})=1$. The partial trace of a tensor product factors by the same finite sums, so $\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}(\rho_{\Lambda'})=\rho_\Lambda$. Thus the local density family is consistent, and [L3] extends it to a state $\eta_\ell$ on $\mathcal A$.

The state $\eta_\ell$ is invariant under shifts in $\ell\mathbb Z^d$ because these shifts permute identical block factors, using the covariance and action law [F6]–[F7]. Average its $\ell^d$ translates over residues $r\in\{0,\ldots,\ell-1\}^d$ to obtain $\omega_\ell=\ell^{-d}\sum_r\eta_\ell\circ\tau_r$. The group law in [F6] makes each lattice translation permute the residue classes modulo $\ell$, so $\omega_\ell\in\mathcal S_{\mathrm{inv}}$.

For each fixed phase $r$, the restriction of $\eta_\ell\circ\tau_r$ to $Q_L$ is a tensor product of full block densities and partial-block marginals. In each coordinate, $Q_L$ contains $L/\ell+O(1)$ full intervals of length $\ell$, so the number of full blocks is $L^d/\ell^d+O_\ell(L^{d-1})$. Entropy additivity in [L2] gives the full-block contribution, while every partial marginal has nonnegative entropy by the opening finite-density spectral calculation in the proof of [F2]; hence $\liminf_{L\to\infty}S_{Q_L}(\eta_\ell\circ\tau_r)/L^d\ge s(\rho_\ell)/\ell^d$. At each finite $L$, concavity in [L2] gives $S_{Q_L}(\omega_\ell)\ge\ell^{-d}\sum_r S_{Q_L}(\eta_\ell\circ\tau_r)$. Divide by $L^d$, take the limit on the invariant left side using [F2], and use the finite number of phases to obtain $s(\omega_\ell)\ge s(\rho_\ell)/\ell^d$.

Put $r=\lceil R\rceil$. By the phase average and translation covariance [F7], $u_\Phi(\omega_\ell)=\ell^{-d}\sum_{x\in Q_\ell}\sum_{S\in\mathscr S_\Phi}\eta_\ell(\Phi(S+x))$. Because each anchored shape contains $0$, the terms with $S+x\subseteq Q_\ell$ sum exactly to $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_\ell H_\ell)$. Every remaining pair $(S,x)$ has $x\in D_{\ell,r}:=\{y\in Q_\ell:\operatorname{dist}_\infty(y,\mathbb Z^d\setminus Q_\ell)\le r\}$, since the support contains $x$ and has diameter at most $R$. If $r=0$, no support crosses a block face and $D_{\ell,0}=\varnothing$. If $r\ge1$, a union bound over the $2d$ faces gives $|D_{\ell,r}|\le2dr\ell^{d-1}$. Terms anchored in these layers may use partial block marginals of $\eta_\ell$; those marginals are positive trace-one by steps 1.2–3.1, and [F5] gives $|\eta_\ell(A)|\le\|A\|$ for each local term. At each anchor the sum of term norms is at most $J_\Phi\le\kappa$ by [F8]. Hence $|u_\Phi(\omega_\ell)-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_\ell H_\ell)/\ell^d|\le2dr\kappa/\ell$. By the equality case of [L1], $s(\rho_\ell)-\beta\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_\ell H_\ell)=\log Z_{Q_\ell}(\beta)$. Hence $s(\omega_\ell)-\beta u_\Phi(\omega_\ell)\ge p_{Q_\ell}(\beta)-2\beta dr\kappa/\ell$.

Take any sequence of positive integers $\ell_j\to\infty$. By [F2], a subsequence of $\omega_{\ell_j}$ converges pointwise to some invariant algebraic state $\omega_*$. The right side of step 5.1 tends to $p_\Phi(\beta)$ by [F1], while step 1.1 bounds every variational value above by $p_\Phi(\beta)$. Thus the sequence of variational values converges to $p_\Phi(\beta)$. Upper semicontinuity of $s$ and continuity of $u_\Phi$ from [F2] imply $s(\omega_*)-\beta u_\Phi(\omega_*)\ge p_\Phi(\beta)$; step 1.1 gives the reverse inequality. Therefore equality is attained, proving the maximum formula.

derivations.claim: At each site, the only possibly nonzero interaction term containing it is its singleton term, and that term has operator norm $|c|$. Every possibly nonzero support is a singleton, so this interaction is translation invariant, has support-size bound $M=1$, range $R=0$, and uniform per-site norm bound $\kappa=|c|$.

Each term $cI_{\{x\}}$ embeds into $\mathcal A_\Lambda$ as $cI_\Lambda$. Therefore $H_\Lambda=c|\Lambda|I_\Lambda$, and the dimension formula gives $Z_\Lambda(\beta)=q^{|\Lambda|}e^{-\beta c|\Lambda|}$. Thus $|\Lambda|^{-1}\log Z_\Lambda(\beta)=\log q-\beta c$ for every finite nonempty $\Lambda$; this same value is the limit along every van Hove sequence. For $c=0$ it is $\log q$, and for $q=1$ it is $-\beta c$.
